newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Copper consumption just above supply Jan-June - ICSG.
newsitem.headline: Copper consumption just above supply Jan-June - ICSG.

text.p: World copper output increased in the first half of 1996 compared with the same period last year but a rise in copper consumption since January has resulted in a gradual decrease in stocks, the Lisbon-based International Copper Study Group (ICSG) said on Thursday.
Mine and refined copper production were 7.9 percent and 6.3 percent higher respectively compared with first half 1995, the ICSG said in a statement released ahead of its August bulletin.
Refined copper recovered from secondary materials was three percent lower than the equivalent 1995 period, it said.
Refined copper consumption was only 1.2 percent higher compared with the same 1995 period but has increased more than 4 percent since January.
The ICSG said world consumption for the six months was 6.16 million tonnes while total refined production was 6.07 million.
The four-week world refined copper consumption rate for the first six months of 1996 was 947,000 tonnes.
Refined copper inventories at the end of June were around 1.06 million tonnes, compared with 1.1 million at the end of May, and down by almost 140,000 tonnes since the end of January.
The average LME spot price for May, 1996 was $2,658 per tonne. For June and July it was lower at $2,173 and $1,990 respectively.
